text: Relation to D5-2 [on paper]. An element of $D_7(G)\setminus\gamma_4(G)$ in a class-4 group gives $1\ne x\in D_5(Q)$ for the class-3 quotient; $x$ has 2-power order, and a finitely generated nilpotent group is residually a finite $p$-group on its $p$-elements (Gruenberg †), so $x$ survives in a finite 2-group of class $\le3$ with $D_5\ne1$: a negative answer to D5-2 (Kourovka 20.84). So the gap closed here is exactly an instance of D5-2; the 80 groups $Q$ (three of them, Rf15, Rf16, Rd46f15, finite 2-groups of class 3) all have $D_4=1$, stronger than the $D_5=1$ that D5-2 asks for. They are instances, not evidence of a general argument.

text: Lemma 3 [on paper]. (i) $\psi:A_4\to\Delta^4/\Delta^n$, $k\mapsto k-1$, is a homomorphism ($(k-1)(k'-1)\in\Delta^8$). (ii) For $K\subseteq A_4$ and $v\in M$: $v\in D_n(M/K)\iff v-1\in\Delta^n+(K-1)A$, and $$(K-1)A+\Delta^n=\Delta^n+\sum_{k}\psi(k)\cdot R,\qquad R=\mathrm{span}\{1\}\cup\{(x_{j_1}-1)\cdots(x_{j_l}-1):1\le l\le n-5\},$$ $k$ over generators of $K$ ($K$ is central, $\psi(k)\Delta^{n-4}\subseteq\Delta^n$, and $\Delta/\Delta^{n-4}$ is spanned by those monomials). Proof. The kernel of $\mathbb Z[M]\to\mathbb Z[M/K]$ is $(K-1)A$, and $\Delta(M/K)^n$ is the image of $\Delta^n$. For $k=\prod k_j^{e_j}$, $\psi(k)\equiv\sum e_j\psi(k_j)$ by (i). $\square$

text: So for a fixed $K$ the question $w\in D_n(M/K)$ is linear: add the rows $\psi(k_j)\cdot r$ to $J_n(M)$. The existence of some $K$ is not: with $\Lambda(k\otimes r)=\psi(k)r$, a $K$ works iff some solution $(k_r)_r\in A_4^{R}$ of $\sum_r\psi(k_r)r\equiv\psi(w)$ (an affine coset of $\ker\Lambda$) has $w\notin\langle k_r\rangle$. "The coordinates of a point of a coset generate a subgroup that misses $w$" is a union over the subgroups $K$ (equivalently over $\varphi\in\widehat{A_4}$ with $\varphi(w)\ne0$), not an intersection: dually, a counterexample is a $\varphi$ that is not of the form $\varphi=\chi\circ\Lambda(\cdot\otimes1)$ for a character $\chi$ of $A/J_n$ with $\chi\circ\Lambda\in\langle\varphi\rangle\otimes\widehat R$ — a rank-one condition on a tensor, which is not linear in $\chi$. This is where a single linear problem stops. What does survive is one-sided:

text: Proposition 4 [on paper]. Let $U_n=J_n+\Lambda(A_4\otimes R_+)$, $R_+$ the monomials of degree $1..n-5$, and $\bar\psi:A_4\to A/U_n$. If $\bar\psi$ is injective, then $D_n(M/K)\cap\gamma_4(M)/K=1$ for every $K\subseteq A_4$. Proof. If $v\in D_n(M/K)\cap A_4$, $v\notin K$, then by Lemma 3 $\psi(v)\in J_n+\psi(K)+\Lambda(K\otimes R_+)\subseteq U_n+\psi(K)$, so $\bar\psi(vk^{-1})=0$ for some $k\in K$, and $v=k\in K$. $\square$

text: $\ker\bar\psi$ is torsion: $\Lambda(A_4\otimes R_+)\subseteq\Delta^5$, so $z\in\ker\bar\psi$ gives $z\in D_5(M)\subseteq\sqrt{\gamma_5(M)}=\tau(M)$ (Jennings), so it is enough to test the elements of order 2 of $\tau(A_4)$ (all of them at once: socle_bits $=$ their number); injectivity found modulo $2^{32}$ is exact (as in (a)). Since $\ker\bar\psi_{n+1}\subseteq\ker\bar\psi_n$, injectivity at $n$ gives it at every larger $n\le8$.

text: Conclusion [computer + on paper, Proposition 4, Corollary 2, (a)]. For every $K\subseteq\gamma_4(M)$, $M=\Gamma/\gamma_5(\Gamma)\Gamma''$ with $\Gamma$ the plateau presentation (3.12): $D_7(M/K)=1$. That is, no metabelian group of class 4 of the form $\Gamma/N$ with $\gamma_5(\Gamma)\Gamma''\subseteq N\subseteq\gamma_4(\Gamma)\gamma_5(\Gamma)\Gamma''$ has $D_7\ne1$ — all central modifications of the plateau group at once, including all $\varphi$ that §6.6 did not try. Likewise $D_5(M/K)=1$ for every $K$ for the 56 bases T and S ($D_5$ also for L1x2, L1x4), and $D_6(M/K)=1$ for the 7 bases L. The enumeration of $\varphi$ in §6.6 for these bases was therefore not a sample but complete.
